papers.title: Geoneutrinos (and reactor neutrinos) do not visibly decay
papers.abstract:
Neutrinos that decay on their way to a detector arrive depleted, more so at low energies, where time dilation lengthens their lifetime the least. Geoneutrinos---electron antineutrinos from the radioactive decay of uranium and thorium inside the Earth---have energies of a few MeV and travel up to the diameter of the Earth. We use them to test neutrino decay for the first time. We compute the geoneutrino signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO for visible decay, in which the daughter neutrinos are themselves detected, and compare it against their published data. We find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models. Combining the four experiments, we limit the decay $
u_1 	o 
u_3$ in the inverted mass ordering at 90% C.L.: $	au_1/m_1 > 3.7 	imes 10^{-9}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when the radiogenic power of the Earth is left free and $	au_1/m_1 > 4.4 	imes 10^{-9}$ to $1.6 	imes 10^{-8}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when it is taken from Earth models. With an Earth model assumed, the geoneutrinos set the limit; with the power free, the antineutrinos from nuclear reactors that the same experiments detect count as much as the geoneutrinos. These are the first terrestrial limits on the visible decay of $
u_1$.

summary.tldr: The first search for visible decay of $\nu_1$ using geoneutrinos and reactor $\bar{\nu}_e$ at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO sets a 90% C.L. limit $\tau_1/m_1 > 3.7 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s/eV}$.
summary.novel_idea: This paper presents the first search for BSM neutrino decay utilizing geoneutrinos, taking advantage of their low energies (few MeV) and long terrestrial baselines (up to Earth's diameter). It builds a detailed visible decay framework that includes energy-dependent daughter flux regeneration across eight decay channels. The analysis fits published prompt energy spectra from four major liquid scintillator experiments under three bulk silicate Earth models as well as with free radiogenic heat power.
summary.method: The author computes two-body decays $\nu_i \to \nu_j + \phi$ incorporating matter oscillations and exact spectral regeneration of daughter neutrinos. Binned Poisson likelihood fits are performed on published prompt positron energy spectra from Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO, treating 75 background, energy scale, mixing, and geochemical parameters as nuisances. Lower limits on $\tau_i/m_i$ are extracted via profile likelihood ratios at 90% and 95% C.L.
key_results: Sets the first terrestrial limit on the visible decay $\nu_1 \to \nu_3$ in the inverted mass ordering: $\tau_1/m_1 > 3.7 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ at 90% C.L. with Earth radiogenic power left free.

With bulk silicate Earth models assumed, the combined 90% C.L. limit strengthens to $4.4 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ (geodynamical Earth) up to $1.6 \times 10^{-8}\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ (cosmochemical Earth).
Establishes that geoneutrinos dominate the $\nu_1$ decay limit under fixed Earth models, whereas reactor $\bar{\nu}_e$ contribute equally when radiogenic power is unconstrained.

Sets bounds on $\nu_2$ and $\nu_3$ decays primarily via reactor antineutrinos (notably JUNO), yielding $\tau_2/m_2 > 1.5 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ and $\tau_3/m_3 > 1.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ s eV}^{-1}$ with free Earth power.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts low-energy neutrino phenomenology, geoneutrino physics, and BSM decay searches. Provides concrete terrestrial baseline bounds that complement astrophysical/cosmological constraints and informs low-energy systematic studies at DUNE, JUNO, and SNO+.
summary.caveats: Limits vary by a factor of 3–4 across different bulk silicate Earth models, and KamLAND's mild deficit of geoneutrinos produces a localized $2.7\sigma$ preference for decay under the geodynamical Earth model.

papers.title: On the cosmic window for neutrino self-interactions
papers.abstract:
Neutrino self-interactions ($
u$SI) beyond the Standard Model have arisen as a promising probe of new physics in cosmology. In this Letter, we show that $
u$SI emerging in the low-energy limit of renormalizable theories implies resonant mediator behavior. We identify two regions for $
u$SI: (i) neutrinos become tightly coupled with background evolution; for the first time, we establish how this evolution modifies the Boltzmann hierarchy equations (BHEs), and (ii) resonant $
u$SI dominates the dynamics with negligible background evolution, relevant for mediator masses $\sim 10^{-6}-1$ MeV. In region (i), before matter-radiation equality, neutrino free-streaming is determined by the effective four-fermion interaction, known as the heavy-mediator limit (HML); we explore the impact of background evolution on this scenario, and from our modified BHEs, we show that self-interacting dark radiation scenarios require larger couplings than previously estimated to mimic $
u$SI. Region (ii) shows that the simplest realization of $
u$SI mediated by a (pseudo)scalar particle leads to an extra radiation contribution of $\Delta N_{m eff}^{m CMB} \approx 0$, instead of the commonly quoted $\simeq 0.12$, at the CMB epoch. Overall, we highlight that our findings should be considered in any plausible scenario involving $
u$SI.
papers.reason: Squarely in the reader's core interest: neutrino phenomenology and new physics.

summary.tldr: A self-consistent cosmic neutrino self-interaction ($\nu$SI) framework incorporating non-zero background collision terms shows resonant mediators yield $\Delta N_{\text{eff}}^{\text{CMB}} \approx 0$ and tighter coupling bounds.
summary.method: Linear perturbation BHEs in conformal Newtonian gauge are modified by introducing background energy density evolution parameters ($\Delta_i$). Neutrino scattering and inverse decay rates are calculated in the complex-mass scheme with the narrow-width approximation. Cosmological perturbation signatures on the CMB TT power spectrum are evaluated using an effective relaxation-time approximation (eRTA) implemented within CLASS.
key_results: Demonstrates that scalar-mediated resonant $\nu$SI leads to $\Delta N_{\rm eff}^{\rm CMB} \approx 0$ at the CMB epoch, in contrast to the canonical $\Delta N_{\rm eff} \simeq 0.12$ derived under fluid approximations.

Delineates two distinct cosmological $\nu$SI regimes: (i) tightly coupled background evolution before equality, and (ii) pure resonant scattering with negligible background evolution for mediator masses $M \sim 10^{-6}\text{--}1\text{ MeV}$.
Finds that CMB TT spectrum enhancements from resonant $\nu$SI are most pronounced for mediator masses $m_\phi \lesssim 1\text{ keV}$.
Shows that self-interacting dark radiation models matching $\nu$SI phenomenology require larger couplings ($\lambda_{\phi\chi}$) than previously estimated due to reduced scalar energy densities.
summary.why_it_matters: Extremely relevant for BSM neutrino interactions, Majoron/light mediator models, and cosmological constraints on non-standard interactions (NSI/$\nu$SI). Corrects standard literature assumptions about $\Delta N_{\text{eff}}$ and background evolution in Boltzmann solvers.
summary.caveats: Perturbative power spectra rely on an effective relaxation-time approximation (eRTA), and full numerical implementation of momentum-dependent background evolution within CLASS remains to be finalized.

papers.title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $\delta_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $\beta$ decays
papers.abstract: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $\alpha$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $\epsilon_\chi$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $\delta_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $\beta$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_\chi^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals. The relative size of three-nucleon corrections to $\delta_{\text{NS}}$ in medium mass nuclei, where two-body contributions tend to be smaller, remains to be investigated. We then use these results to determine $V_{ud}$ from the superallowed transition ${}^{10}\mathrm{C}\rightarrow{}^{10}\mathrm{B}$.
papers.reason: Squarely in the reader's core interest: nuclear EFT, electroweak processes, and precision physics. [favorite author: Saori Pastore]

summary.tldr: Derives $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_chi^2)$ three-nucleon potentials for $\bar{\delta}_{\text{NS}}$ in superallowed $\beta$ decay, showing $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ 3N terms shift $V_{ud}$ by $\sim 10^{-4}$ while $\mathcal{O}(\alpha\epsilon_chi^2)$ corrections are $\sim 2\%$.
summary.novel_idea: The paper derives the full set of three-nucleon (3N) electroweak radiative correction potentials at order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_chi^2)$ in chiral effective field theory for the nuclear-structure-dependent correction $\bar{\delta}_{\text{NS}}$. Using CVC and current algebra, the authors explicitly prove that vector-vector (VV) 3N contributions cancel out, leaving only vector-axial (VA) operators to be evaluated in nuclear matrix elements.
summary.method: Using Heavy Baryon Chiral Perturbation Theory (HB$\chi$PT), 21 electroweak 3N diagrams are derived and reduced via CVC constraints. Variational and Green's Function Monte Carlo (VMC/GFMC) methods with Norfolk chiral two- and three-nucleon interactions (NV2+3) are used to compute 3N matrix elements for ${}^6\text{He}\to{}^6\text{Li}$ and ${}^{10}\text{C}\to{}^{10}\text{B}$. The extracted matrix elements are used to re-evaluate $V_{ud}$ from ${}^{10}\text{C}$.
key_results: Proves that vector-vector (VV) 3N radiative corrections cancel identically via CVC, leaving only vector-axial (VA) 3N operators for $\bar{\delta}_{\text{NS}}$.
Computes $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ 3N matrix elements, showing they scale as $Z^2$ and shift $V_{ud}$ by $\sim 10^{-4}$, demonstrating their necessity for precision CKM unitarity tests.

Evaluates $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_chi^2)$ 3N matrix elements in ${}^{10}\text{C} \to {}^{10}\text{B}$, finding a small $\approx 2\%$ correction to $\bar{\delta}_{\text{NS}}$, confirming good chiral EFT convergence.
Extracts an updated value of $V_{ud} = 0.97386(61)$ from the superallowed ${}^{10}\text{C}$ Fermi decay, shifting it closer to neutron decay determinations.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts precision electroweak physics, beta decay radiative corrections, CKM $V_{ud}$ unitarity, chiral EFT electroweak operators, and ab initio QMC calculations of electroweak responses.
summary.caveats: Calculations of $\mathcal{O}(\alpha \epsilon_chi^2)$ 3N contributions were performed only for light nuclei (${}^{10}\text{C}$); their relative magnitude in medium-mass nuclei ($A \ge 14$), where two-body magnetic terms are suppressed, remains to be calculated.

papers.title: Producing $\mu$Bq/m3-level low-226Ra ultrapure water for the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory
papers.abstract: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), a 20 kton low-background liquid-scintillator (LS) detector, was designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. JUNO requires ultrapure water (UPW) with a Ra concentration < 50~$\mu$Bq/m3 because of the direct liquid-liquid contact between LS and UPW during detector filling. To meet this stringent requirement, a high-sensitivity measurement system capable of detecting Ra in water down to 3.9 $\mu$Bq/m3 was developed, and the 100 t/h UPW production process was optimized. By integrating selective ion-exchange resin with membrane-based separation technologies, the system consistently produced UPW with a Ra concentration of <4$\mu$Bq/m3, exceeding the JUNO specification and, to our knowledge, representing one of the lowest reported levels achieved at this engineering scale. This paper describes the design and implementation of JUNO's UPW system and the high-sensitivity Ra measurement platform, together with a systematic evaluation of Ra removal efficiencies across the purification train and validation of the final water quality.
papers.reason: Directly relevant to the reader's interest in low-energy neutrino physics, specifically background reduction for DUNE/JUNO-like experiments.

summary.tldr: JUNO's 100 t/h ultrapure water system achieves a Ra-226 concentration of $<4\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$, exceeding the experiment's $<50\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$ background requirement.
summary.novel_idea: Reports the design, engineering, and performance of JUNO's 100 t/h ultrapure water (UPW) system, which achieves an ultra-low ${}^{226}\text{Ra}$ concentration of $<4\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$. A custom assay system based on Mn-fiber adsorption and radon emanation was developed, attaining an unprecedented measurement sensitivity of $3.9\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$ for radium in water.
summary.method: The purification process combines multi-media filters, dedicated cationic softening resin, and two-stage reverse osmosis (RO). ${}^{226}\text{Ra}$ concentration is measured by concentrating radium on synthesized Mn-fibers, transferring emanated ${}^{222}\text{Rn}$ into an electropolished chamber, and counting alpha decays from ${}^{214}\text{Po}$ via electrostatic collection detectors over 24-hour acquisition windows.
key_results: Reduced water ${}^{226}\text{Ra}$ concentration from $\sim 4 \times 10^5\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$ in raw source water to $<4\ \mu\text{Bq/m}^3$ in product UPW ($>99.999\%$ overall reduction).
Determined that cationic softening resin and two-stage RO each independently achieve $>99\%$ ${}^{226}\text{Ra}$ removal efficiency.
Identified sea-salt regenerant sediment in softening tanks and unfiltered air ingress through tank breather valves as the main post-purification recontamination pathways.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant as background baseline context for JUNO low-energy neutrino, geoneutrino, and supernova physics. However, the content is purely experimental facility engineering and detector instrumentation.
summary.caveats: High-resistivity water sampling data was incomplete due to sensor hardware limitations, and complete tank cleaning operations require future system shutdowns.

papers.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. Supported by numerical evaluations, this framework establishes OPEC and OPCC angular widths as sensitive probes of higher-twist dynamics and fundamental properties of cold nuclear matter.
papers.reason: Highly relevant to the reader's interest in QCD resummation, hadronization, and nuclear medium effects in scattering.

summary.tldr: Establishes the first proof of NLO QCD twist-4 factorization for OPEC and OPCC angular widths in semi-inclusive DIS off nuclear targets.
summary.novel_idea: The paper delivers the first formal proof of next-to-leading order (NLO) collinear QCD factorization for twist-4 power corrections to one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-nucleus semi-inclusive DIS ($e+A$ SIDIS). It proves that medium-enhanced final-state soft and collinear singularities cancel completely, proving IRC safety at twist-4.
summary.method: The authors apply the higher-twist expansion framework to compute NLO real and virtual double-scattering diagrams in $e+A$ SIDIS. They calculate medium-induced transverse momentum broadening of the angular spread $\Delta \langle \sin^2 \theta \rangle$ and express the factorization in terms of nuclear matrix elements $T_{qg}(x,x_g)$ and fragmentation moments.
key_results: Proves explicit cancellation of all medium-associated final-state soft and collinear divergences at twist-4 NLO for OPEC and OPCC angular spreads.
Demonstrates that fragmentation function dependence reduces strictly to universal momentum ($M_q=1$) and charge ($M_q=Q_q$) moments.
Shows numerically that nuclear angular broadening grows linearly with nuclear size ($A^{1/3}$) and exhibits characteristic $1/Q^2$ power suppression.
Finds that OPCC broadening is smaller than OPEC due to the decoupling of charge-neutral gluons in charge-weighted correlators.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to lepton-nucleus/electron-scattering interactions, QCD factorization, nuclear medium effects, and cold nuclear matter studies for the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).
summary.caveats: Numerical predictions incorporate only diagonal soft rescattering matrix elements; off-diagonal hard rescattering matrix elements remain unconstrained by existing nuclear data.

papers.title: Gravitational Form Factors and Transverse Mechanical Structure of the Charged Kaon in a Two-Fock-Sector Light-Front Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We study the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors of the charged kaon in a light-front Hamiltonian model with coupled $|u\bar s\rangle$ and $|u\bar s g\rangle$ Fock sectors. We solve the coupled Hamiltonian in a longitudinal Jacobi and transverse harmonic-oscillator basis, with the interaction strength fixed by the kaon mass. The momentum form factors are extracted from $T^{++}$, while the stress form factors are obtained from the transverse shear projection of the QCD Belinfante energy-momentum tensor, including diagonal, sector-changing, and constrained-field contributions. The strange antiquark carries the largest fraction of the kaon's longitudinal momentum, whereas the gluon carries only $2.05\%$. Despite this small momentum fraction, the gluon contributes $42.4\%$ of $|D_K(0)|$, for which we obtain $D_K(0)=-2.03610$. The charge and transverse momentum radii are $0.5178\pm0.0278\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.3394\pm0.0113\,\mathrm{fm}$, respectively, with uncertainties estimated from mass and basis variations. We obtain the transverse mechanical distributions using two ultraviolet continuations of the directly calculated $D$ form factors beyond $Q^2=2\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$. Both continuations give positive pressure at small transverse distances and negative pressure at larger distances. The corresponding transverse mechanical radii are $0.4616\pm0.0130\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.4768\pm0.0132\,\mathrm{fm}$, both larger than the transverse momentum radius. The central pressure changes substantially between the two continuations, whereas the pressure zero and mechanical radii vary much less.
papers.reason: Directly relevant to the reader's core interest in nucleon/hadron form factors and mechanical structure.

summary.tldr: Charged-kaon electromagnetic and gravitational form factors are calculated in a light-front Hamiltonian with coupled $|u\bar{s}\rangle$ and $|u\bar{s}g\rangle$ Fock sectors, finding gluons carry only $2\%$ momentum but contribute $42\%$ to the $D$-term.
summary.novel_idea: The work extends light-front Hamiltonian meson gravitational form factor calculations beyond the valence sector by including an explicit dynamical gluon Fock sector. This enables resolving the separate quark, antiquark, and gluon contributions to momentum and shear distributions using a projected Belinfante energy-momentum tensor that includes diagonal, sector-changing, and constrained-field contact terms.
summary.method: The coupled $|u\bar{s}\rangle \oplus |u\bar{s}g\rangle$ Hamiltonian is solved by Rayleigh-Ritz projection onto longitudinal Jacobi and full-plane transverse harmonic-oscillator bases, with coupling calibrated to the physical kaon mass. Momentum form factors are computed from $T^{++}$ overlaps in the Drell-Yan frame, while the mechanical $D$ form factor is extracted from the off-diagonal transverse shear $T^{12}$. Two rational UV continuations beyond $Q^2 = 2\text{ GeV}^2$ are matched to evaluate 2D Fourier-Bessel transverse pressure and shear profiles.
key_results: Forward momentum form factors at $\mu_0 = 0.58\text{ GeV}$ are $A_u(0) = 0.354$, $A_{\bar{s}}(0) = 0.625$, and $A_g(0) = 0.0205$, showing strange-quark momentum dominance.
Obtains $D_K(0) = -2.03610$, with the gluon carrying $42.4\%$ of the total mechanical term despite carrying only $2.05\%$ of the longitudinal momentum.
Calculated charge radius is $r_{\text{ch}} = 0.5178 \pm 0.0278\text{ fm}$ and transverse momentum radius is $r_{A,\perp} = 0.3394 \pm 0.0113\text{ fm}$.
Transverse mechanical radii are $0.4616 \pm 0.0130\text{ fm}$ (Ansatz 1) and $0.4768 \pm 0.0132\text{ fm}$ (Ansatz 2), demonstrating that central pressure is highly sensitive to the UV completion.
Both UV continuations yield positive internal pressure at small transverse distance and negative pressure at outer radii, fulfilling mechanical stability.
summary.why_it_matters: Although kaon mechanical structure is peripheral to neutrino-nucleus cross sections, the treatment of multi-sector light-front wavefunctions, operator overlap contractions, and EMT matrix elements provides reference methodology for hadronic matrix element calculations.
summary.caveats: The model omits dynamical sea-quark pairs ($|u\bar{s}q\bar{q}\rangle$), and the transverse pressure at small impact parameter depends significantly on the chosen rational UV continuation above $2\text{ GeV}^2$.

papers.title: $\Lambda$-deuteron scattering below the $\Sigma$-threshold
papers.abstract: $\Lambda d$ elastic scattering and breakup below the $\Sigma$ threshold is described fully including the virtual coupling to $\Sigma$ channels. Well-converged results are obtained solving the multichannel scattering equations for three-body transition operators in momentum-space. Scattering length, exclusive, semi-inclusive and total elastic and breakup cross sections, and spin observables are calculated, aiming to study their dependence on kinematic variables and dynamic ingredients. The uncertainty due to the hyperon-nucleon interaction model is most sizable. The observables and regimes that could help to constrain the hyperon-nucleon force models are identified. The single-channel approximation of the problem is validated at low and intermediate energies.
papers.reason: Directly relevant to the reader's interest in neutrino-nucleus interactions and hyperon-nucleon forces.

summary.tldr: Multichannel three-body AGS equations are solved in momentum space for $\Lambda d$ scattering below the $\Sigma$ threshold, identifying observables sensitive to hyperon-nucleon forces and validating single-channel approximations at low energies.
summary.novel_idea: This paper presents the first fully converged momentum-space calculation of $\Lambda d$ elastic scattering, breakup reactions, and spin observables below the $\Sigma$ threshold that fully retains the four-sector Hilbert space $(\Lambda pn \oplus \Sigma^+ nn \oplus \Sigma^0 pn \oplus \Sigma^- pp)$ across all relevant partial waves ($J \le 39/2$). It rigorously assesses the validity of the widely used single-channel approximation where $\Sigma$ channels are truncated in three-body equations.
summary.method: Alt-Grassberger-Sandhas (AGS) multichannel integral equations are solved directly in the momentum-space partial-wave basis for three-body transition operators. Nuclear dynamics are modeled using chiral N3LO and CD-Bonn $NN$ potentials alongside NLO chiral EFT $YN$ potentials (NLO19) with cutoffs varied from $500$ to $700\text{ MeV}$, including screened Coulomb interactions in the closed $\Sigma^- pp$ channel.
key_results: Doublet $\Lambda d$ scattering length is moderately model-independent ($18\text{--}21\text{ fm}$), whereas the quartet scattering length varies dramatically ($-9.5$ to $-30.7\text{ fm}$) due to a virtual-state pole near threshold.
The $\Lambda d$ breakup cross section exhibits a sharp increase approaching the $\Sigma$ threshold driven by a resonant $J^\Pi = 1/2^+$, isospin-1 state.

Semi-inclusive proton momentum and angular spectra feature prominent peaks from quasi-free $\Lambda n$ scattering around $E_p \approx 14\text{ MeV}$, providing a sensitive probe of unmeasured $\Lambda n$ forces.

Neglecting $\Sigma$ coupling in three-body equations is accurate within $10\text{--}20\%$ at low and intermediate energies, but breaks down severely near the $\Sigma$ threshold (up to $90\%$ deviations in elastic backward angles).
summary.why_it_matters: Provides rigorous few-body scattering techniques for extended Hilbert spaces; the exact multichannel AGS solutions and chiral EFT potential benchmarks are directly analogous to three-body continuum methods used in nuclear electroweak response theory.
summary.caveats: The calculations omit explicit three-body hypernuclear forces ($YNN$), and experimental $\Lambda d$ scattering data remain insufficient for direct potential calibration.

papers.title: Radii of Sn Isotopes near the Proton Dripline from Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory
papers.abstract: We present the first $\textit{ab initio}$ lattice calculations of charge and matter radii of tin isotopes $^{96}$Sn, $^{98}$Sn, $^{100}$Sn, $^{102}$Sn and $^{104}$Sn near the proton dripline using nuclear lattice effective field theory with high-fidelity two- and three-nucleon forces combined with the partial-pinhole algorithm. The resulting radii are larger then predicted from other ab-initio methods. We find that variations of the three-nucleon interaction reveal substantial radius differences even among interactions with similar binding energies. We intensively discuss of the role of different choices of the three-body forces.
papers.reason: Directly relevant to the reader's interest in nuclear structure and ab initio methods.

summary.tldr: Nuclear lattice EFT with wavefunction matching and the partial-pinhole algorithm provides the first ab initio predictions of charge and matter radii for proton-dripline tin isotopes $^{96\text{--}104}\text{Sn}$.
summary.novel_idea: This work achieves the first ab initio nuclear lattice EFT calculations of both charge and matter radii for heavy nuclei near the proton dripline ($A \sim 100$), specifically $^{96}\text{Sn}$ through $^{104}\text{Sn}$. It combines wavefunction matching with the partial-pinhole algorithm and systematic variations of partial-wave-resolved 3N interactions to establish radius-energy correlations in heavy systems.
summary.method: Simulations are performed using Euclidean-time lattice projection with spatial spacing $a = 1.32\text{ fm}$ in an $L=14$ box ($La = 18.48\text{ fm}$). The Hamiltonian incorporates an N3LO two-nucleon interaction with wavefunction matching to suppress sign oscillations, coupled to partial-wave-resolved 3N forces. Radii are extracted via two-body density correlations from a 12-particle partial pinhole, fully including Galilean invariance restoration (GIR) corrections.
key_results: Extracted charge radii for $^{96\text{--}104}\text{Sn}$ are systematically larger by $\approx 0.1\text{--}0.2\text{ fm}$ than Bogoliubov coupled-cluster results using EM(1.8/2.0) potentials, but consistent with self-consistent Green's functions with NNLOsat.

GIR corrections shift charge radii downward by $\sim 0.08\text{ fm}$ at $A \sim 100$, demonstrating an approximate linear scaling with $A$ that outpaces the naive phenomenological $A^{1/3}$ expectation.

Variations in 3N interactions that produce identical binding energies in light nuclei yield substantial spreads in tin radii, showing that radii in heavy nuclei provide independent constraints on 3N low-energy constants.
Extrapolated two-neutron separation energies $S_{2n}$ show a sharp step drop of $\approx 11\text{ MeV}$ across $N=50$, correctly capturing the shell closure.
summary.why_it_matters: Constraining 3N forces and charge radii via ab initio lattice EFT informs the nuclear ground-state distributions and nuclear-EFT inputs that underpin electroweak current matrix elements in medium and heavy nuclei.
summary.caveats: Calculations are conducted at a single lattice spacing without continuum extrapolation; sign oscillations restrict Euclidean projection time for $^{104}\text{Sn}$ to $\tau \le 0.8\text{ MeV}^{-1}$, leading to sizable extrapolation uncertainties.

papers.title: Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC
papers.abstract: Quantum information observables in top quark pair production have opened a new experimental window on non-classical correlations of particle interactions at colliders. Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering occupies a distinguished place in the quantum hierarchy, lying between entanglement and Bell nonlocality. We present a detailed collider analysis of steerability for top quark pairs at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). In particular, we utilize both the decay and kinematic methods to estimate the expected sensitivity of the LHC and High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to detect steerable states. We find that with the current LHC dataset of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ the steerability of the $t\bar t$ state in the boosted region can be established at $7.7\sigma$ ($1.8\sigma$) in the semileptonic (dileptonic) channel with the decay method, corresponding to a measurement of the steerability integral at a precision of $1.5\%$ ($5.2\%$), while the kinematic method reaches a precision of $0.05\%$ in both channels. At the HL-LHC the decay-method precision improves to $0.3\%$ ($1.1\%$). Near threshold, where the inclusive selections used for entanglement and discord yield a state at the steerability boundary, an optimized selection $M_{t\bar{t}}\lesssim360$--$400$~GeV isolates a steerable singlet-dominated state, where the sensitivity is projected to reach $7\sigma$ ($3.4\sigma$). We also provide a detailed discussion on the interpretation of these results with respect to fictitious quantum states, and argue for the robust nature of the steerability measurement at colliders.
papers.reason: Relevant to the reader's interest in quantum entanglement and spin correlations in scattering final states, even if applied to top quarks. [favorite author: Tao Han]

summary.tldr: Collider measurement of EPR steering is formulated for top-quark pairs at the LHC, establishing a convex criterion for fictitious states and projecting $7.7\sigma$ observation in the boosted semileptonic channel with current data.
summary.novel_idea: The paper establishes the theoretical and experimental framework for measuring Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering at colliders. Crucially, it proves that the steerability integral is convex in the spin correlation matrix, guaranteeing that a steerable fictitious state reconstructed in the event-by-event helicity basis rigorously certifies genuine steerable quantum substates across phase space without requiring local hidden state assumptions.
summary.method: Leading-order $pp \to t\bar{t}$ events at $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ TeV}$ are simulated with MadGraph5, MadSpin, Pythia8, and Delphes3 in both semileptonic and dileptonic channels. The spin density matrix is reconstructed via decay angular asymmetries (unfolded with RooUnfold) and kinematic template methods. Closed-form analytic steering criteria are derived in terms of singular values of the spin correlation matrix, and fiducial phase space cuts are optimized for threshold and boosted regimes.
key_results: Derived exact lower and upper bounds on the steerability integral $\mathcal{S}$, yielding a sufficient steering condition $\sum_i \mu_i > 3/2$ and a necessary condition $\text{tr}(C^T C) > 3/4$.

Established that steerability occupies an intermediate window in top pair invariant mass: for transverse $gg \to t\bar{t}$, steering occurs for $M_{t\bar{t}} < 386\text{ GeV}$ and $M_{t\bar{t}} > 770\text{ GeV}$, strictly between entanglement and Bell-nonlocality thresholds.

In the boosted region ($M_{t\bar{t}} > 800\text{ GeV}$), steerability can be observed at $7.7\sigma$ ($1.8\sigma$) in the semileptonic (dileptonic) channel with $139\text{ fb}^{-1}$ via the decay method, achieving $1.5\%$ precision on $\mathcal{S}$.
The kinematic method achieves $0.05\%$ precision on $\mathcal{S}$ in both channels with $139\text{ fb}^{-1}$.

HL-LHC ($3\text{ ab}^{-1}$) projections reach $0.3\%$ ($1.1\%$) precision in the boosted semileptonic (dileptonic) channel and enable a $7.0\sigma$ discovery in an optimized threshold singlet region ($M_{t\bar{t}} \le 360\text{ GeV}$).

papers.title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter (DM) can form hydrogen-like bound states around black holes (BHs), that can be perturbatively described at small gravitational fine-structure constant alpha=G*M*mu<<1, where M and mu are the masses of the BH and the DM scalar, respectively. We show that self-interactions lead to the formation of a 2p-halo around a Schwarzschild BH, with the final cloud density as high as 10^5 times the background density. We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH. Consequently, the 211 cloud mass is bounded from above by M_{211}^{crit}/M~=5*10^{-3}*alpha^{-1/2}*[f_a/10^{16} GeV]^2 up to an O(1) factor depending on the spin of the BH. Crucially, for rapidly spinning BHs with M~<4*10^6 M_{sun}, alpha~<0.03, and f_a~<9*10^{15} GeV the resulting superradiant cloud mass is lower than previously assumed, which might have an impact on axion bounds from measurements of stellar BH spins.

summary.tldr: Quartic self-interactions allow ultralight scalar dark matter to form dense $2p$ halos around Schwarzschild black holes and impose a critical mass ceiling on superradiant clouds around spinning Kerr black holes.
summary.novel_idea: The authors discover that quartic self-interactions allow ultralight dark matter to form long-lived excited $2p$ bound halos around Schwarzschild black holes through Bose-enhanced capture, circumventing the rapid absorption that destabilizes the $1s$ ground state. Furthermore, for spinning Kerr black holes, the self-interaction-induced transition $211 + 211 \to 100 + k$ populates the ground state and caps superradiant $211$ cloud growth earlier than previously assumed.
summary.method: Gross-Pitaevskii field equations are solved perturbatively in the gravitational coupling $\alpha = GM\mu \ll 1$ up to second order in the scalar self-interaction $g = \mu^2/f_a^2$. Matrix elements coupling hydrogenic bound states ($1s, 2s, 2p$) and Coulomb scattering states are evaluated numerically via Monte Carlo integration with importance sampling. The resulting coupled rate equations are evolved using an adaptive Euler integrator across focusing parameters $\xi = (v_{\text{DM}} \alpha)^{-1}$ and decay constants $f_a$.
key_results: Identified distinct halo regimes around Schwarzschild black holes: no-halo ($\xi \lesssim 1$), $1s$-dominated, intermediate ($2p \to 2s$ suppression), and dilute/dense $2p$ halos (stabilized by $2p \to 1s$ decay).
The equilibrium $2p$ halo reaches local overdensities up to $10^5$ relative to the ambient background DM density, though the total halo mass remains bounded below $10^{-12} M_{\text{BH}}$.
For Kerr black holes, $211 \to 1s$ decay sets a critical ceiling on the superradiant cloud mass: $M_{211}^{\text{crit}} / M \approx 5 \times 10^{-3} \alpha^{-1/2} (f_a / 10^{16}\text{ GeV})^2$.

For rapidly rotating black holes with $M \lesssim 4 \times 10^6 M_\odot$, $\alpha \lesssim 0.03$, and $f_a \lesssim 9 \times 10^{15}\text{ GeV}$, superradiant growth saturates early, potentially relaxing axion parameter exclusions derived from stellar black hole spin measurements.

papers.title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
papers.abstract: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_\eta(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-\eta_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. Its vacuum part is a dimension-four, CPT-even Lorentz-violating term of the Standard Model Extension with coefficient $(\cL)_{ii}=-\eta_0(m_i^2-m_1^2)/(2E_0^2)$, diagonal in the mass basis and fixed by the mass matrix, hence removable by a reparametrization. The matter-potential rescaling has dimension-five behaviour and is CPT-odd. For $f=1-\eta_0(E/E_0)^p$ the vacuum term behaves as a dimension $p+2$ operator and the matter term as $p+3$, so only $p=2$ gives a marginal vacuum operator; $p=0$ is absorbed into the measured mass splittings, and non-integer $p$ admits no local operator. For $\eta_0=0.02$ at $E_0=2.5$~GeV we find $|(\cL)_{33}|\simeq4\times10^{-24}$, comparable to present atmospheric bounds, whereas a Planck-suppressed deformation with $\beta_0=\mathcal{O}(1)$ gives $3.2\times10^{-58}$. At constant density it is equivalent to $L\to f(E)L$: mixing angles and the Dirac phase are unchanged, the CP asymmetry is reparametrized rather than generated, and the leading observable is a rescaling of $\dm_{31}$. At $1297$~km a re-fit of $\dm_{31}$ alone absorbs $23$~per cent of the squared probability difference, and a four-parameter re-fit absorbs $41.5$~per cent. No statistical analysis is performed; degeneracy means a distance in probability space, not a confidence interval.

papers.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
papers.abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

papers.title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
papers.abstract: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(\xi, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. At the model input scale, only valence quarks are included. With the vertex correction, the electromagnetic form factors $G_{E, M}$ and the mass form factor $A$ obtained from the Mellin moments of the GPDs agree well with those obtained from direct calculations. The vertex correction brings the evolved charge weighted distribution $\sum{e^q E^q(\xi, x, t)}$ closer to the phenomenological parametrization. The correction shifts transverse strength from the central region toward the peripheral region, consistent with the long range character of the pion cloud contribution. The transverse structure results further suggest a harder longitudinal momentum distribution in the central region of the nucleon than in its periphery. Furthermore, the evolved real part of the proton Compton form factor, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}(\xi, t)$, has a reasonable magnitude and follows the main trend of the Quantum Deep Neural Networks (QDNN) extraction. In addition, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}$ may be more sensitive to the ERBL region than the other physical quantities calculated in this work.

papers.title: Precision Measurements of the Effective Leptonic Weak Mixing Angle at Hadron Colliders
papers.abstract: We review precision determinations of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle, $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$, from Drell-Yan angular asymmetries at the Tevatron and the LHC. As statistical uncertainties have dramatically decreased, parton distribution function (PDF) uncertainty now dominates the most precise hadron-collider results. We describe the angular observables, electroweak calculation schemes, and advanced methods such as replica reweighting and Hessian profiling, used to constrain PDFs directly from measured angular distributions. To identify the origin of differences between modern PDF sets (e.g., CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF) in the extracted mixing angle, we employ a simplified leading-order Z-pole calculation that separates quark-flavor production weights from quark-direction dilution. We demonstrate how these PDF-induced differences can be mitigated by incorporating complementary constraints from W/Z cross-section ratios and W-boson decay asymmetries. Furthermore, we discuss the requirements for a common reinterpretation and future combination of LHC measurements, highlighting how correlated PDF uncertainties limit the ultimate combined precision. Finally, we outline future prospects, including complementary measurements in $Z+b$ production and high-mass tests of the running $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ weak mixing angle.

papers.title: Density functional theory of renormalization group in nuclear matter
papers.abstract: We present the density functional renormalization group (density-fRG), in which density fluctuations are separated from the quantum fluctuations in the vacuum and are integrated out successively within the functional renormalization group approach. This allows us to quantify medium effects and to study the physics of high baryon densities. The method is applied to the nucleon-meson effective field theory, also known as the Walecka model, where the density dependence of the nucleon-meson Yukawa couplings is generated self-consistently by their flow equations. It is found that both the attractive and the repulsive nucleon-meson interactions are screened by the dense medium. This results in an equation of state of symmetric nuclear matter that is stiffer than in the relativistic mean-field approximation for $\rho_0\lesssim\rho\lesssim 2.5\,\rho_0$, and becomes softer for $\rho\gtrsim 2.5\,\rho_0$, where $\rho_0$ is the saturation density. Furthermore, a new phenomenon called the locking of the Fermi surface is found: the effective energy of the quasi-nucleon stays close to the Fermi surface, while both are running with the renormalization group scale.

papers.title: Pole parameters of the $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from a coupled-channel analysis of the radiative $J/\psi$ multipoles
papers.abstract: We determine the pole parameters of $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from the combined fit to the isoscalar $D$-wave $\pi\pi$ phase shift, the $\pi\pi\to K\bar K$ modulus, and the BESIII $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0$ and $\gamma K_SK_S$ data: all three $2^{++}$ multipoles $E1$, $M2$ and $E3$, and the $M2$-$E1$ phases. The hadronic amplitude is a two-channel $K$-matrix with two poles and all parameters free, so that no resonance information is taken from the Particle Data Group. The radiative decay amplitudes are written as a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representation, with the Omn\`es matrix generated by that hadronic amplitude. The left-hand cuts, which carry the production dynamics, are approximated by a linear subtraction polynomial in the physical region. The model-independent kinematic constraints among the $J=2$ helicity amplitudes are implemented explicitly. The fit describes all $358$ points with $\chi^2/N=1.29$ and gives $\sqrt{s_p}=(1267.5\pm1.3\pm2.6)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(175.5\pm2.4\pm7.4)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2(1270)$ and $(1514.8\pm2.8\pm1.5)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(80.4\pm3.4\pm4.8)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2'(1525)$, where the first uncertainty is statistical, from a parametric bootstrap with the data errors rescaled by $\sqrt{\chi^2/N}$ of each set, and the second systematic, from $17$ variations of the analysis.

papers.title: Isospin effects and symmetry energy in nuclear reactions
papers.abstract: Isospin and the symmetry energy are linked within the symmetry term of the liquid-drop mass formula and within the corresponding term of the equation of state of asymmetric nuclear matter. The Pauli exclusion principle leads to a leading quadratic dependence of the kinetic part of the symmetry term of the nuclear binding-energy formula on the neutron-proton asymmetry (N-Z)/A. Charge symmetry ensures the same leading quadratic dependence for the potential part. Charge invariance further generalizes this dependence, to lowest order, from T$_3^2$ to T(T+1). The strength of the symmetry term, in contrast, is determined by the symmetry energy. At sub-saturation densities the symmetry energy can be constrained by nuclear-structure observables, such as neutron skin thicknesses, isovector collective modes and the related electric dipole polarizability, and excitation energies of isobaric analog states. It can also be constrained by reaction observables, such as charge exchange and elastic scattering cross sections, isoscaling and isospin diffusion. At supra-saturation densities, by contrast, the only means of studying asymmetric nuclear matter under laboratory conditions are relativistic heavy-ion collisions. These studies use differential observables such as neutron/proton flows and light isobar or $\pi^{-}/\pi^{+}$ ratios. Complementary information can be obtained from neutron star observations including gravitational waves. The latest measurements and analyses of the stiffness of the symmetry energy will be presented, together with the recent NA61/SHINE observation of an unexpectedly large isospin-symmetry violation in kaon production. Attention will also be paid to the challenges of measuring charged and neutral products of relativistic heavy-ion collisions in the context of the recent ASY-EOS II experiment at GSI and to the new detectors used in the setup.

papers.title: Study of the intra-pixel timing resolution of planar silicon sensors using the TDCpix ASIC
papers.abstract: A study of the intra-pixel timing resolution in planar silicon detectors, bonded to the TDCpix Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), is performed using the TimePix4 telescope. Spatial non-uniformities in the timing resolution, arising from the weighting field, are measured for the first time in an experimental environment. papers.title: First observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed decay $B^+_c \to J/\psi D^{\ast+}$
papers.abstract: The first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed decay $B^+_c \to J/\psi D^{\ast+}$ using proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment between 2011 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $9\,\rm{fb^{-1}}$, is presented. The result is used to test theoretical models of two-body hadronic decays of $B^+_c$ mesons and agrees with several predictions in the literature.

papers.title: Role of excited hyperons in $K^{*}\Xi$ production via $K^{-}N$ scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the production mechanism of $K^-N\to K^*\Xi$ and the role of high-mass excited hyperons within an effective Lagrangian approach, using a combined fit to cross section and polarization data for $K^-p\to K^{*+}\Xi^-$. The model includes $s$- and $u$-channel exchanges of the ground-state $\Lambda$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons, together with $s$-channel contributions from $\Lambda(2325)$ and $\Sigma(2230)$. The pronounced near-threshold enhancement of the total cross section is driven mainly by these excited hyperons, whereas $u$-channel exchange dominates at backward angles at higher energies. Polarization results show that both the $K^*$ spin-density matrix elements and the $\Xi$ recoil polarization are sensitive to excited-hyperon contributions near threshold. Notably, the latter remains sensitive to interference involving excited-hyperon amplitudes even at higher energies. Moreover, with the same fitted parameters and no additional free parameters, the predicted cross sections for $K^-p\to K^{*0}\Xi^0$ and $K^-n\to K^{*0}\Xi^-$ agree well with available measurements. Finally, a Dalitz analysis of $K^-p \to K^{*+}\Xi^- \to K\pi\Xi^-$, together with existing $K\pi\Xi^-$ cross section data, indicates the feasibility of reconstructing $K^{*+}\Xi^-$ through this final state. These results suggest that $K^*\Xi$ production provides a valuable reaction channel for investigating high-mass excited hyperons and their hadronic couplings, and offers theoretical guidance for future experimental measurements.

papers.title: Probing dimension-six SMEFT operators in heavy-quark sector at future muon collider
papers.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity to the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators which define the interactions of heavy-quarks with electroweak gauge bosons and with leptons via the process $\mu^- \mu^+ \rightarrow Wtb$, followed by leptonic W-boson decays, at a 10 TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of 10 ab$^{-1}$. Signal and background events are generated at leading order using MadGraph5aMC@NLO, interfaced with Pythia 8 for parton showering and hadronization, and passed through Delphes 3.5 for fast detector simulation. The 95% confidence level (C.L.) limits on nine Wilson coefficients are derived using a cut-based method for two $b$-tagging working points (70% and 90% efficiencies). These limits are significantly tighter than those currently reported by the CMS Collaboration; furthermore, these results highlight the advanced potential of a future high-energy muon collider to investigate new physics within the electroweak sector through precise measurements of heavy-quark interactions.

papers.title: Improving Sensitivity to Rare Processes at the LHC with Geodesic-Aware Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Rare processes at the Large Hadron Collider often lead to final states with quarks, for which the dominant backgrounds contain the same reconstructed objects as the signal. The colour structure of the hard process, imprinted on the pattern of soft QCD radiation, carries information that is largely left unused by standard analyses. We introduce a geometric representation of this colour flow by mapping hadronic constituents onto the unit sphere through a modified inverse stereographic projection centred on a pair of jets selected as a colour-singlet resonance candidate. The jet separation defines a circular region whose interior and exterior are mapped to opposite hemispheres, allowing a graph neural network to exploit the resulting radiation pattern using geodesic distances. As a benchmark, we consider flavour-changing neutral interactions of the top quark with the Higgs boson at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$~TeV, through associated $tH$ production and $t\bar t$ production with one top quark undergoing a $t\to qH$ decay, where $q=u,c$, focusing on subsequent $H\to b\bar b$ and leptonically top quark decays in both channels. Relative to a baseline graph neural network operating in the $(\eta,\phi)$ plane, the geodesic-aware network improves the expected 95\% confidence-level limits on $\mathrm{BR}(t\to uH)$ and $\mathrm{BR}(t\to cH)$ by about an order of magnitude, to $1.1\times10^{-4}$ and $8.3\times10^{-5}$ for an assumed integrated luminosity of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The approach can also be applied to searches for other colour-singlet resonances decaying into quarks or gluons.

papers.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
papers.abstract: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

papers.title: A fully differential charged-particle phase-space measurement of $Z$+jets production in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
papers.abstract: The production of a $Z$~boson decaying to muons in association with hadronic jets is a benchmark process in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. It provides a clean experimental signature with high selection efficiency and purity while probing a wide range of Standard Model dynamics. Measurements of this process are typically reported as binned differential cross sections in a limited set of predefined observables, which reduces the information retained and hinders reinterpretation. In this paper, the OmniFold method is used to produce an unbinned and highly differential measurement of the $Z$+jets cross section using 140 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector. This constitutes the first published unbinned, fully differential measurement of a collider cross section, describing the kinematics of individual charged particles within a well-defined region of phase space. This unbinned event representation is used to construct measurements in four example applications that illustrate the broad range of observables constrained with a single measurement, including several that would be difficult or impossible to access using traditional unfolding methods. The measurement is published as particle-level Monte Carlo events together with unfolded event weights, allowing arbitrary observables to be constructed after publication and enabling a broad range of future applications and reinterpretations.

papers.title: Hadronic production of excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC
papers.abstract: We study the hadronic production of ground-state and excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC for $\sqrt{S}=13$ TeV within the framework of NRQCD factorization at leading order in QCD. The calculation includes the $1S$, $1P$, and $2S$ multiplets, with both color-singlet and color-octet contributions to direct $1P$ production. For $p_T>0.2$ GeV, the summed production cross section is $336.04^{+275.80}_{-175.43}$ nb; the quoted uncertainty combines the specified heavy-quark mass and common-scale variations and does not include PDF-set differences. The NNPDF3.0 and MSHT20LO predictions are approximately $23\%$--$24\%$ below the CT18LO result. With the adopted radiative-transition branching fractions, $2S$ feed-down increases the total $1P$ yield from $34.73$ to $75.34$ nb. The relative enhancement differs markedly among the four spectroscopic states, ranging from $38\%$ for $1^1P_1$ to $262\%$ for $1^3P_0$, and it reorders their integrated production hierarchy. Within the set of states included here, the ratio of the $1P$ yield to the inclusive ground-state yield increases from $0.103$ to $0.224$. We present the state-resolved distributions and the dependence of direct production on kinematic cuts, parton distributions, quark masses, and scale choices. These results illustrate the potential impact of $2S$ feed-down on the relative yields of the lowest $P$-wave $B_c$ states.

papers.title: No room for $X(2370)$ exceptionalism: the glueball interpretation warrants caution
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/\psi$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/\psi\to\gamma PPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\eta^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $\eta(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $\eta_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0\eta$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: Active Learning and Genetic Search for Discrete Abelian Flavor Model Building
papers.abstract: The sequential breaking of discrete flavor symmetries provides a theoretical framework that can explain quark mass and mixing angle hierarchies. Each model is identified by its field content, charge assignments and symmetry breaking pattern, leading to an enormous space of possible models; this motivates the investigation of computational approaches for identifying promising candidates. In this work, we focus on quark flavor models with the flavor symmetry group $G_F=(\mathbb{Z}_2)^p$, where $p$ is a positive integer; operators involving flavon fields which spontaneously break the flavor symmetry determine the size of the Yukawa matrix entries. We consider two search strategies: an active learning search employing a random forest regressor and a genetic search. The generation of candidate models is automated and models are evaluated using a loss function that takes into account the logarithmic discrepancy between the model prediction and target observable values as well as penalties for model complexity. We find that both our active learning and genetic algorithms significantly outperform random model generation, which we use as a control; our active learning approach identifies lower-loss models faster (i.e., with fewer exact model evaluations) than our genetic search, though each ultimately finds successful models. Our results support the effectiveness of active learning and evolutionary optimization as approaches to automate the search for promising models based on discrete flavor symmetries.

papers.title: A New GUT
papers.abstract: We present a new class of 4-dimensional Grand Unified Theories where the gauge sectors of the standard model have a novel embedding in the unified group that does not factor through an $SU(5)$ subgroup. The smallest example has gauge algebra $\frak{su}(12)$ and an anomaly-free spectrum that produces the three standard model generations with no additional chiral matter. The embedding predicts the axion-photon anomaly ratio $E/N=2/3$ and the weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_W=1/2$ at the unification scale. Gauge-mediated proton decay proceeds through flipped-$SU(5)$-like operators and the minimally charged smooth monopole carries two Dirac charge units. The global gauge group can be $SU(12)$ or $SU(12)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, with the former allowing color singlets of half-integer electric charge. We develop a GUT bootstrap to constrain $SU(n)$ embeddings with three generations and no additional chiral matter. For unified fermions in up to two-index representations, we prove that all new embeddings arise from the $SU(8m+4)$ family, including flavor unified models for $m \geq 2$.

papers.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the E\"otv\"os parameter is $\eta\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $\alpha\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $\lambda\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

papers.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
papers.abstract: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.

papers.title: The Price of Discovery: Cost-Optimized Detectors for the GUT-Scale QCD Axion
papers.abstract: Grand unification and string theory point to a quantum chromodynamics (QCD) axion with mass between $10^{-11}$ and $10^{-8}$ eV, while heterotic string theory suggests a mass of $0.5-0.8$ neV. We study which laboratory experiment could discover or exclude DFSZ-strength QCD axion dark matter at and above 0.5 neV at the lowest cost, which we estimate from scaling laws calibrated to historical data. We find that a lumped-element detector, building on the ABRACADABRA concept, can do so with demonstrated readout technology; an example is a shielded toroid about 14 m across with a 6 T NbTi magnet, whose magnet and cryostat we estimate at around 120 million Swiss francs (MCHF). If projected readout targets are met, a 5 m toroid at 25 MCHF suffices. We find these designs by optimizing the toroid, solenoid, and core lumped-element topologies under a common cost metric. The toroid emerges as the most promising and cost-effective topology. The optimal field of the toroid detector is far below the 16 T of the proposed DMRadio-GUT design, which would cost nearly twice as much as our optimum. Heterodyne searches with superconducting radio-frequency cavities, with cavity shapes that we optimize for price, cost between about the same as and twice as much as the lumped-element detectors, but require cavities of volumes $\sim50-2000$ m$^3$. We find that nuclear-magnetic-resonance searches (CASPEr) need orders-of-magnitude gains in spin polarization and coherence. We release axionMultiPhysics, an open-source finite-element and multiphysics package for, e.g., magnetoquasistatic and full-wave electromagnetics, superconductors, readout circuits, and mechanics, from which most of our numerical results were obtained.

papers.title: Leading Axion Sensitivity with Interstellar Medium Optical Line Emission
papers.abstract: We introduce interstellar optical line emission as a new probe of axion dark matter. Axion decays to photons or electrons can excite or ionize neutral hydrogen, producing H$\alpha$ emission at a fixed atomic wavelength rather than at an energy set by the axion mass. Developing the formalism and applying it to the Leo T galaxy with Very Large Telescope data, we derive strong constraints for eV--GeV scale axions, covering new regions of parameter space for both axion-photon and axion-electron couplings. These results establish optical line measurements as a new discovery channel for axion dark matter, probe poorly constrained parameter space below hydrogen's ionization threshold, and constrain axion explanations of JWST's high-redshift supermassive-black-hole observations.

papers.title: Cold Magnetized Quark Matter under Compact-Star Conditions
papers.abstract: We investigate the phase structure of cold magnetized two-flavor quark matter under compact-star conditions within a nonlocal chiral quark model with separable interactions. Electric charge neutrality and beta equilibrium are imposed in order to describe matter under realistic neutron-star conditions, while nonlocality is implemented through a Gaussian form factor. We find that low and moderate magnetic fields reduce the critical chemical potential for chiral symmetry restoration, signaling inverse magnetic catalysis. For stronger magnetic fields, the critical chemical potential becomes nearly independent of the magnetic field strength, Compared with the isospin-symmetric case, the combined effects of charge neutrality and beta equilibrium shift the first-order chiral transition to slightly higher chemical potentials, indicating that compact-star constraints delay the onset of chiral symmetry restoration. We further show that charge neutrality and beta equilibrium modify the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in the quark density, shifting the Landau-level thresholds for the $u$ and $d$ quarks in opposite directions relative to the isospin-symmetric case. The effect on the chiral transition is small ($\sim 5$MeV) for fields $B\lesssim 10^{19}$G, relevant for magnetar interiors, and becomes sizable only for $B\gtrsim 3\times10^{19}$G. These results highlight the importance of incorporating realistic stellar conditions in studies of the QCD phase diagram at high baryon density.

papers.title: Effects of charm-strange resonances on charmed meson production by recombination in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract: We discuss charmed mesons in heavy-ion collisions by focusing on their production from the quark-gluon plasma by quark recombination. We consider the production of not only the $D$, $D^*$, $D_s$, and $D_s^*$, but also the $D_{s0}^*(2317)$, $D_{s1}(2460)$, $D_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_{s2}^*(2573)$, thereby investigating the important role of heavier charm-strange resonances in understanding the measurements of the $D$ and $D_s$ mesons at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We calculate their yields and transverse momentum distributions, and also evaluate ratios of the transverse momentum distribution between various charmed mesons, i.e., the $D_s$ and $D^0$, the $D_s$ and $D^+$, $D_s^*$ and $D^{*0}$, and $D_s^*$ and $D^{*+}$. Through this analysis, we attempt to understand in more detail the effects of strangeness enhancement on charmed meson production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$ TeV.

papers.title: Deployment of a Graph-Based Track Seeder for the ATLAS Phase-II Tracking Upgrade
papers.abstract: The ATLAS experiment is undergoing significant detector, computing and software upgrades for the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC). The ongoing software modernisation is essential to leverage future processing technologies and ensure maintainability throughout the operation of the experiment, while meeting the tracking performance requirements for physics and reducing the compute needs for event reconstruction. To meet these goals, the ATLAS Collaboration is adopting the ACTS (A Common Tracking Software) toolkit, an experiment-independent software for charged-particle track reconstruction. Using ACTS in the ATLAS reconstruction software at the HL-LHC facilitates the development and integration of new algorithms while promoting thread safety, high performance, and code maintainability. This document describes the development and recent deployment of a Graph-Based Track Seeder (GBTS), its underlying methodology, and its expected tracking performance at the HL-LHC.

papers.title: Total Angular Momentum Assignments in the Hadron Spectrum
papers.abstract: Predicting the total angular momentum $J$ for hadronic resonances whose spins have not yet been experimentally determined constitutes an important step in the spectroscopy of observed hadrons. In the present study, we develop a data-driven model in order to predict the value of $ J $ for hadrons with unknown spins using a dataset of known mesons and baryons from the PDG, including information on their quark content, isospin, parity, mass and other spectroscopic features. In particular, we employ XGBoost classifiers along with nested optimization in order to discover spectroscopic patterns across different hadronic sectors. We also prepare a systematic list of hadrons with unknown or poorly determined values of $ J $, and study spin-parity assignments for those hadrons. Since the parity hypothesis is taken as an input to the model, our model predicts the value of $ J $ conditional on a given parity hypothesis rather than independently determining the full $J^P$ assignment. Our predictions for several theoretically studied states show good agreement with results from quark models, QCD sum rules, molecular models, and other phenomenological approaches, while predictions for some other states differ from existing theoretical assignments. These differences motivate further theoretical investigations and may be tested by future experimental measurements.

papers.title: A high-resolution search for axion dark-matter flows with ORGAN-Q
papers.abstract: We search for narrow axion dark-matter flows using the high-resolution data acquired during the ORGAN-Q experiment. The analysis covers nine potential axion linewidths from 0.466$~$Hz to 119.209$~$Hz, equivalent to axion effective quality factors $1.3\times 10^{10}$ to $5.2\times 10^7$, over the range 6.1550$~$GHz to 6.3496$~$GHz, corresponding to axion masses of approximately 25.455$~\mu \mathrm{eV}$ to 26.260$~\mu \mathrm{eV}$. Once contributions from native-bin correlations, data-quality and interference vetoes, frequency-dependent system noise, the cavity response, and filter attenuation are accounted for, no candidate satisfies the required persistence ratio in any search bandwidth. Across the nine assumed linewidths, the strongest $95\%$ KSVZ axion-flow density limits range from 22.8$~\mathrm{GeVcm^{-3}}$ for a $0.466~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal to $153.7~\mathrm{GeVcm}^{-3}$ for a $119.209~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal, with both attained near $m_a=25.857~\mu \mathrm{eV}$.

papers.title: The ALICE asynchronous software trigger processing for LHC Run 3
papers.abstract: The detector and computing upgrades for LHC Run 3 enable ALICE to continuously acquire proton--proton (pp) and lead--lead (Pb--Pb) collisions at interaction rates of up to 1.5 MHz and 50 kHz, respectively. The resulting pp dataset is more than three orders of magnitude larger than the combined Run 1 and Run 2 samples, and its long-term retention in full would be impractical given the available storage capacity. To address this challenge, ALICE has implemented a physics-driven asynchronous software trigger designed to retain only collisions containing signals of physics interest. Following full asynchronous reconstruction, the Central Event Filter Processor applies more than 100 analysis-based selection channels spanning the ALICE pp physics programme. The selected collisions are then used to skim the original Compressed Time Frames (CTFs), preserving the relevant detector information within detector-specific time windows. This procedure reduces the retained CTF volume to approximately 4.5% of its original size, while preserving the possibility of future reconstruction with improved calibrations and software. This contribution describes the implementation and operation of the asynchronous software trigger, from collision selection to CTF skimming, and highlights how this strategy provides access to rare signals and processes across the ALICE physics programme.

papers.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
papers.abstract: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $\rho$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

papers.title: Coupled-channel pole structure and bare-state mixing of bottom-strange heavy-quark spin partners
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of the $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ and the heavy-quark symmetry relations connecting the $DK$, $D^*K$, $\bar{B}K$, and $\bar B^*K$ systems, we investigate whether the same chiral dynamics can generate negative-parity partners dominated by the $\bar B_1K$ and $\bar B_2^*K$ components. We further examine how nearby bare bottom-strange states reshape the pole spectrum through coupled-channel mixing. Both the relevant $S$-wave scattering and the lower-lying $P$-wave decay channels are explicitly included in the coupled-channel calculation. In the absence of bare states, the interaction generates two negative-parity poles near $6.15$ GeV. Coupling the hadronic channels to the corresponding quark-model configurations leads to a richer two-pole structure in each sector, with the pole masses, widths, and channel residues governed by the interplay between the bare states and the hadronic dynamics. In particular, the inclusion of the bare states substantially increases the widths of the negative-parity poles with the larger $S$-wave molecular components. The resulting correlated patterns in the pole spectrum provide testable signatures for future studies of excited bottom-strange mesons.

papers.title: Long-lived linear slow roll near critical and spinodal points in soft-wall AdS/QCD
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the real-time evolution of the chiral condensate near critical and spinodal points within soft-wall AdS/QCD, focusing primarily on the long-lived prethermalization stage, in contrast to the conventional early transients and late-time relaxation. While the quasi-steady nature of this stage has been previously identified, we demonstrate that it is intrinsically a continuous linear slow roll, fundamentally distinct from the asymptotic critical slowing down at late times. By showing that the bulk evolution adiabatically follows the boundary condensate on a slow configuration space, we analytically project the 5D partial differential equation onto a boundary first-order Ginzburg-Landau (GL) equation. We find that the long lifetime of this linear regime is protected by a ``double-zero'' condition: the simultaneous vanishing of the local potential gradient (suppressing the drift velocity) and curvature (suppressing the acceleration). This geometric flatness inherently emerges at the second-order point and both first-order spinodal endpoints. Crucially, this behavior is not a fine-tuned artifact, but a generic consequence of the effective potential landscape intrinsic to these phase-transition endpoints, persisting across a broad class of physically relevant initial conditions and temperature quenches. A local short-time expansion further relates the interval duration to the potential curvature and its higher-order derivatives, in good agreement with our numerical simulations. This work establishes a direct link between the local structure of phase-transition endpoints and the dynamical evolution of the long-lived intermediate stage of the condensate.
